input: This memo considers whether maintenance sensors should be installed across the plant's pump population, and what the evidence currently available actually supports. The plant runs 260 pumps in total, and maintenance records covering a period of 12 months show a substantial 1333 h of unplanned downtime, of which bearing failures alone account for 46% of the downtime hours. A sensor set covering all 260 pumps has been quoted at $441k installed, plus a further $66k per year in ongoing costs. In a trial conducted by the vendor on a comparable unit, the sensors were reported to cut downtime by 20%, although it is important to note that this figure is a vendor figure and has not been measured at this plant. It should also be noted that spare-part lead times are completely unaffected by the sensors. Rather than committing the full $441k on the strength of a vendor figure, it is recommended that a three-month pilot be carried out first, covering 16 pumps at a cost of $43k. The pilot would be owned by the reliability engineering group, which would report its findings before the March capital review, and the decision on full installation would be held until those results are available. The pilot, at $43k, would replace the vendor's claim with a measurement made on the plant's own pumps.
target: The recommendation is a three-month pilot of maintenance sensors on 16 pumps, at $43k, with the decision on full installation held until the pilot results are reported. The reliability engineering group owns the pilot and reports before the March capital review. The plant runs 260 pumps. Maintenance records for 12 months show 1333 h of unplanned downtime, and bearing failures account for 46% of the downtime hours. A sensor set for all 260 pumps is quoted at $441k installed, plus $66k per year. In a vendor trial on a comparable unit, the sensors cut downtime by 20%; the figure is a vendor figure and was not measured at this plant. Spare-part lead times are unchanged by the sensors. The pilot substitutes a plant measurement for the vendor figure on the failure mode with the largest share of the downtime, and it prices that substitution at $43k against a full-installation quote of $441k committed on the vendor figure alone. A pilot result that matches the vendor figure supports the full installation at the capital review; a result below it reprices the case on plant data. The pilot report is the document the capital review decides on, and the review date is fixed by the pilot's reporting line rather than by the currency of the quote.
